nodes.body: Please use the existing runtime-compilation test infrastructure, e.g. gtests like `gtest/handle_test.cpp` or `gtest/miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp`, instead of a standalone hipRTC test.

Thanks for the guidance — the regression test now lives in MIOpen's existing gtest runtime-compilation infrastructure and the standalone binary plus its manual CMake registration are gone (commit 1d2481cf; the two smaller thread comments are addressed in 1845028f).

**Design.** `test/gtest/hiprtc_selfcontained.cpp` registers `CPU_HipRtcSelfContained_NONE.RtCompilesBatchNormWithoutHostStl` through the normal gtest glob (no custom CMake), and compiles the *embedded production* `MIOpenBatchNormFwdTrainSpatial.cpp` through `Handle::AddKernel` — the same pathway `handle_test.cpp` / `miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp` use — so the fix is exercised through its real wiring (option assembly, embedded kernel sources, named-header include map), and the target architecture comes from the live device.

**Keeping the original guarantee.** The host C++ standard library is made unreachable by passing `-nostdinc` (fallback `-nostdinc++`) in the compile options, and a paired probe proves it before any verdict counts: a negative probe that `#error`s when any of `<type_traits>/<utility>/<limits>/<initializer_list>` is still reachable, plus a positive ambient probe that actually uses `<type_traits>`. On a tree where a kernel header regresses to host-STL includes, the runtime compile fails and the test fails. A per-run compile option defeats the kernel-binary cache (keyed by program+options), so a stale cached object can never satisfy it.

**Results (Windows 11, gfx1151, ROCm 7.14 wheel toolchain):**
- patched tree: PASS — probes prove isolation, the BatchNorm kernel compiles with no host STL reachable, the code object loads; the with-STL control also passes;
- unpatched baseline (`54b079ca` + this test): FAILS with the original field signature — `miopen_type_traits.hpp:151: fatal error: 'type_traits' file not found` as the single error — while the same kernel compiles with STL available, i.e. the failure is STL-specific;
- hosts whose runtime compiler injects host STL anyway (e.g. comgr on Linux) skip with an explicit message that the no-STL condition was not tested — never a silent pass; inconsistent probe results fail the test instead of guessing.

One conscious trade vs the standalone: the test now runs through a live `Handle` like the other runtime-compilation gtests, so it needs a GPU present and no longer doubles as a GPU-less compile-only checker. The wheel environment this regression targets always has the GPU; the no-STL condition itself is the compiler environment, recreated by the isolation flags and verified by the probes.

Threads on the comment cleanup and radix.hpp `<limits>` are addressed in 1845028f: `MIOpenKthvalue.cpp` (the only radix.hpp consumer) was recompiled through the production path in both the ambient and STL-isolated quadrants. Happy to adjust anything else.

I suggest renaming `miopen_freestanding_initializer_list.hpp` to `miopen_initializer_list.hpp` and moving the header selection logic into it. Then `tensor_view.hpp` only needs `#include "miopen_initializer_list.hpp"`.

Done: renamed to `miopen_initializer_list.hpp` and moved the header selection into it (real `<initializer_list>` when reachable, freestanding definition otherwise); `tensor_view.hpp` now only includes it and the CMake kernel-header registration was updated (c6ed8131). The fallback layout is unchanged; the regression test brace-constructs `tensor_layout_t` and verifies the written values on GPU.

The `miopen_cstdint.hpp` include doesn't add much on its own here, since `MIOpenKthvalue.cpp` (the only user) already includes it, both directly and via `tensor_view.hpp`, before `radix.hpp`. Including what you use is a good idea, but then I think it would be worth adding the rest as well, e.g. `miopen_type_traits.hpp` for `std::is_same`.

+// Copyright (c) Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., or its affiliates.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+// Regression test: runtime-compiled MIOpen kernels must stay self-contained
+// when the runtime compiler cannot reach a host C++ standard library.
+//
+// On hosts whose clang has no configured C++ stdlib reachable from the
+// runtime-compile path (for example the AMD Windows pip-wheel stacks, or any
+// HIPRTC environment without host STL search paths), kernels pulling
+// <type_traits>/<utility>/<limits>/<initializer_list> through
+// miopen_type_traits.hpp / miopen_utility.hpp / radix.hpp / tensor_view.hpp
+// fail at hiprtcCompileProgram with "'type_traits' file not found". The fix
+// selects freestanding definitions via __has_include when no standard
+// library is reachable.
+//
+// This test compiles the originally failing kernel through the production
+// runtime-compilation path (miopen::Handle::AddKernel with an empty kernel
+// source, so the embedded MIOpenBatchNormFwdTrainSpatial.cpp and the
+// freestanding headers' real named-header registration are exercised) while
+// the host C++ standard library is unreachable: it passes only when that
+// kernel's include closure stays self-contained. On a tree where a kernel
+// header has regressed to requiring host-STL includes, the runtime compile
+// fails and AddKernel raises, failing this test.
+//
+// Why AddKernel and not a standalone hiprtc program: the regression is a
+// property of MIOpen's own runtime-compilation environment (option assembly,
+// embedded kernel sources, named-header include map), and the existing gtest
+// runtime-compilation tests (handle_test.cpp, miopen_cstdint_lp64.cpp) reach
+// it exactly this way.
+//
+// Probing order, each compile through the same production path:
+//   P0  a trivial kernel under the isolation option. If it does not compile,
+//       the toolchain itself is broken under isolation; the test fails as a
+//       setup error rather than guessing about MIOpen sources.
+//   P1  a probe kernel that #errors when any of the four gated standard-
+//       library headers is still reachable. Compiling it under isolation
+//       PROVES the no-STL precondition before any verdict counts.
+//   P2  the same environment without isolation, positively using
+//       <type_traits>. Compiling here means the host standard library is
+//       genuinely usable in the ambient environment (drives the with-STL
+//       control); failing means it is not (e.g. a host with no stdlib at
+//       all, where the with-STL control is not applicable).
+// On hosts where the runtime-compiler environment injects the host STL even
+// under -nostdinc (observed with comgr on Linux), P1 fails while P2
+// compiles: the run reports itself as skipped, stating that the no-STL
+// condition was not tested, never as a pass. P1 failing together with P2
+// means the probes are inconsistent and the test fails rather than
+// misclassifying.
+//
+// Cache freshness: the persistent kernel-binary cache is keyed by program
+// name and options, not by source content, so every compile below carries a
+// unique per-run option and a distinct program name. A stale cached object
+// can therefore never satisfy the regression check (for example after
+// reverting the fix and rebuilding in place).

+constexpr const char* kProgramName = "MIOpenBatchNormFwdTrainSpatial.cpp";
+constexpr const char* kKernelName  = "MIOpenBatchNormFwdTrainSpatial";
+
+// Minimal production-style define set for the BatchNorm spatial kernel
+// (src/solver/batchnorm/forward_spatial.cpp defines the full geometry set;
+// default_configurations.hpp, included by configuration.hpp, provides the
+// defaults for the geometry macros).
+constexpr const char* kBatchNormDfn =

+    " -DMIOPEN_LAYER_NCHW=1 -DMIOPEN_LAYER_NHWC=0 -DMIO_BN_VARIANT=0"
+    " -DMIO_BN_GRP0=1024 -DMIO_BN_GRP1=1 -DMIO_BN_GRP2=1";
+
+// Isolation candidates, strongest first: full -nostdinc is required on
+// msvc-triple clang, whose automatic MSVC STL detection bypasses
+// -nostdinc++; -nostdinc++ keeps libc headers for toolchains whose

+constexpr const char* kIsolationCandidates[] = {"-nostdinc", "-nostdinc++"};
+
+const char* kTrivialKernel = "#ifndef MIOPEN_HIP_RUNTIME_COMPILE\n"
+                             "#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>\n"
+                             "#endif\n"
+                             "extern \"C\" __global__ void gtest_rtc_trivial() {}\n";
+
+// Fails to compile (via #error) exactly when any of the four standard-
+// library headers the freestanding patch gates on is reachable.
+const char* kStlProbeKernel = "#ifndef MIOPEN_HIP_RUNTIME_COMPILE\n"
+                              "#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>\n"
+                              "#endif\n"
+                              "#if __has_include(<type_traits>) || __has_include(<utility>) || "
+                              "__has_include(<limits>) || __has_include(<initializer_list>)\n"
+                              "#error MIOPEN_GTEST_STL_REACHABLE\n"
+                              "#endif\n"
+                              "extern \"C\" __global__ void gtest_rtc_probe() {}\n";
+
+// Compiles exactly when the ambient environment can actually use the host
+// standard library. Inverted polarity versus kStlProbeKernel so that a
+// uniformly broken probe cannot be mistaken for an STL-reachable host.
+const char* kStlUseKernel = "#ifndef MIOPEN_HIP_RUNTIME_COMPILE\n"
+                            "#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>\n"
+                            "#endif\n"
+                            "#include <type_traits>\n"
+                            "static_assert(std::is_integral<int>::value, \"stl usable\");\n"
+                            "extern \"C\" __global__ void gtest_rtc_stl_use() {}\n";
+
+// Generated at execution time (never at build time) so that rebuilds in the
+// same build directory cannot reuse an earlier run's cache entries.
+std::string NonceOption()
+{
+    static const auto stamp = std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch().count();
+    static std::atomic<unsigned> seq{0};
+    return "-DMIOPEN_GTEST_RTC_NONCE=" + std::to_string(stamp) + "_" + std::to_string(seq++);
+}
+
+// Compile `src` through the production runtime-compilation path. AddKernel
+// compiles, loads the module and resolves the kernel symbol eagerly; only
+// the launch is deferred, so a returned invocation means compilation
+// produced a loadable code object containing the named kernel.
+bool Compiles(miopen::Handle& h,
+              const std::string& program,
+              const std::string& kernel,
+              const std::string& params,
+              const std::string& src)
+{
+    try
+    {
+        auto invoke = h.AddKernel("gtest_rtc_regression",
+                                  "",
+                                  program,
+                                  kernel,
+                                  {1, 1, 1},
+                                  {1, 1, 1},
+                                  params + " " + NonceOption(),
+                                  0,
+                                  src);
+        (void)invoke;
+        return true;
+    }
+    catch(const std::exception&)
+    {
+        return false;
+    }
+}
+
+} // namespace

+    std::string isolation;
+    for(const char* candidate : kIsolationCandidates)
+    {
+        if(Compiles(h, "gtest_rtc_trivial.cpp", "gtest_rtc_trivial", candidate, kTrivialKernel))
+        {
+            isolation = candidate;
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+    ASSERT_FALSE(isolation.empty())
